key_insight: LLM agents exposed to a GNN tool mostly stop reasoning independently and instead copy the tool’s prediction, with stronger backbones deferring even more.
engineering_relevance: For agentic ML systems, tool use should be designed as a selective decision policy rather than assumed to emerge from scale or prompting.
method: Freeze a GNN and attach it as an explicit callable tool to a ReAct-style LLM agent.
Evaluate node classification on text-attributed graphs (ogbn-arxiv, replicated on WikiCS).
Sweep LLM backbone size (Qwen2.5 0.5B–7B) and compare agent outputs against raw GNN, alternative tools, and oracle/selective-gating baselines.
evidence_signal: Across 5 seeds, agent predictions agreed with the raw GNN 97.6–99.2% of the time, and agreement increased from 0.60 to 0.98 as backbone size grew from 1.5B to 7B.
watch_item: Selective invocation is constrained by the information available at test time, so better routing logic alone may not overcome the gap to an oracle policy.
paper_title: When the Tool Decides: LLM Agents Defer Blindly to Graph Neural Network Tools, and Stronger Backbones Defer More
